headline: Air Quality Crisis: Dhaka ranks world’s second most polluted city
summary: The capital city faces a severe air pollution crisis, climbing to the second spot globally in terms of air quality.
details: Dhaka has been ranked as the second most polluted city in the world according to recent air quality data.
The city's air quality index often reaches hazardous levels, posing significant health risks to millions of residents.
Major contributors to this pollution include vehicle emissions, construction dust, and industrial waste.
The persistent smog and poor air quality have become a critical environmental and public health emergency for the capital.

topic: extreme heat threatens pregnant women and newborns
headline_marked: Extreme heat [[putting pregnant women and newborns at risk]], UN warns
headline: Extreme heat putting pregnant women and newborns at risk, UN warns
summary: UN Climate Change Executive Secretary Simon Stiell warns that rising temperatures are creating a 'fatal' new faultline in the global climate crisis for mothers and babies.
details: UN Climate Change Executive Secretary Simon Stiell has warned that extreme heat is putting pregnant women and newborns at growing risk as the climate crisis intensifies.
Speaking at the launch of the Birthright campaign in Fiji, Stiell described pregnancy and birth as a 'new faultline' in the global climate crisis that is potentially fatal.

A survey of 1,000 maternal health professionals across Australia, Brazil, India, the UK, and Zimbabwe found that 73% had seen an increase in heat-related complications for pregnant women over the past five years.
The survey revealed that 98% of respondents had cared for a pregnant woman and 99% had cared for a baby whose health they believed was affected by extreme heat.
Data from Wellcome indicates that a 1°C rise in temperature is associated with a 5% increase in premature births and a 7% increase in gestational diabetes.
Stiell noted that exposure to extreme heat is increasingly linked to premature birth, stillbirth, low birth weight, and maternal complications.
He emphasized that 'staying cool' is not an option for those living in unregulated housing or relying on facilities without power or cooling, widening global injustice.
The UN chief called for pregnancy and newborn care to be integrated into climate adaptation plans, alongside stronger alert systems and safer health facilities.
He urged countries to deliver on adaptation finance, calling for $1.3 trillion a year to be made available to developing countries to prevent a 'deep chasm' of suffering.

The survey revealed that 98% of respondents had cared for a pregnant woman and 99% had cared for a baby whose health they believed was affected by extreme heat.

Data from Wellcome indicates that a 1°C rise in temperature is associated with a 5% increase in premature births and a 7% increase in gestational diabetes.

Stiell noted that exposure to extreme heat is increasingly linked to premature birth, stillbirth, low birth weight, and maternal complications.

He emphasized that 'staying cool' is not an option for those living in unregulated housing or relying on facilities without power or cooling, widening global injustice.

The UN chief called for pregnancy and newborn care to be integrated into climate adaptation plans, alongside stronger alert systems and safer health facilities.
